target: A moderation team is deciding whether to roll out a new classifier threshold. In a fresh random audit it made 95 correct decisions out of 100. Policy requires evidence at the 95% confidence level that true decision accuracy is at least 90%; the observed 95% point estimate alone is not an acceptable gate. The team must decide whether this sample clears the rollout policy now.
surface: A previous moderation-classifier rollout used observed audit accuracy as its gate: 95 correct decisions in 100 audited items was displayed as 95% accuracy, and the threshold was rolled out because 95% exceeded the 90% target.
structural: In an election poll, 95 of 100 sampled voters favored a measure. To obtain a 95% lower confidence bound for the underlying favorable proportion, analysts used the Wilson score lower endpoint: (p + z^2/(2n) - z*sqrt(p(1-p)/n + z^2/(4n^2))) / (1 + z^2/n), with z=1.96. They compared that lower endpoint, not p alone, with the required support floor.
rubric: Explicitly selects a one-sided use of the 95% Wilson score lower confidence endpoint rather than the raw proportion alone.
Substitutes p=0.95, n=100, and z=1.96 into the Wilson lower-endpoint calculation.
Computes the lower endpoint as about 0.888 (88.8%).
Concludes the evidence does not clear a 90% minimum and does not recommend rollout now.
Notes that this is a confidence-bound decision about the sampled operating distribution, not proof of all future inputs.
